about.title: Nikos Malakasis
about.bio: I'm a PhD candidate at the Computation in Neural Circuits Lab at TU Munich, led by Prof. Dr. Julijana Gjorgjieva. I build computational models of how excitatory and inhibitory synaptic plasticity shape the subcellular organisation of synapses on dendrites — the branching structures through which neurons receive and integrate signals — and what that organisation means for learning. Beyond research, I supervise master's and bachelor's theses, teach classes, and contribute to grant writing. I hold an MSc in Bioinformatics from the University of Crete (9.4/10) and a BSc in Biology from the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens. Originally from Greece, I've lived and studied across Europe. Athens, Crete, Braga, and now Munich. Outside of work, I'm into video games, generative AI art, graphics design, video editing, martial arts, yoga, snowboarding, strategic board games, trading card games, and anime.

research.org: Computation in Neural Circuits Lab · TU Munich
bullets: Develop spiking and biophysical models of how inhibitory plasticity shapes where synapses sit on dendrites.
Supervised four master's students and one bachelor's student on research projects.
Presented at Bernstein 2023, Cosyne 2024, Dendrites 2024 & 2026, and the Inhibition in the CNS Gordon Research Conference 2025.
Teach classes and assist with grant writing.
Built a bio-realistic Spiking Neural Network in C++ to study how structural plasticity affects image classification.
Worked on designing simplified interneuron models with active dendrites using Brian2.
